query: How does the Sovereign AI memory manager handle concurrent model switch requests?
context_chunks: The C++ fast core memory manager implements a thread-safe single heavy model invariant using Win32 Critical Sections or POSIX mutexes.
When a request requires a model switch (e.g., from chat model to coder model), the memory manager marks the active model as evicting, unloads its VRAM allocation, and loads the target model.
Lightweight CPU-only components like the cross-density reranker and embedding pipelines remain in system RAM (16 GB) without competing for the 8 GB GPU VRAM.
If concurrent requests target different models, the memory manager queues the second request or schedules execution to avoid GPU out-of-memory errors.

query: What security mitigations prevent path traversal in tool calls?
context_chunks: The filesystem tool resolves paths against the project workspace root and asserts Path.is_relative_to(root).
Attempts to access sensitive paths such as /etc/passwd, C:\Windows\System32, or parent traversals (../) trigger a SecurityException and are logged to the audit service.
File upload handlers strip directory components using Path(filename).name to eliminate remote path injection vectors.
